equity_bridge.note: Balance sheet is 30 Sep 2026 and year 1 is FY2027. Q4-2026 adjusted EBITDA ~1,550 (FY guide at least 6,000 less 9M 4,510.1) less remaining net growth capex ~1,790 (guide ~5,000 less 9M 3,213.7) and maintenance ~80; cash tax nil.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 adjusted-EBITDA growth judged from guidance and the project schedule; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.9-4.8%) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (29.8% 3yr) and from adjusted EBITDA (19.6% 3yr). Attributable book equity is not a usable growth anchor here: it is held down by buybacks, dividends and the 1.8bn Badlands noncontrolling-interest repurchase, and FY2020 carries a 2.4bn impairment. Revenue CAGRs are commodity-price noise (FY2022 was the price peak). EPS 5yr is not meaningful (FY2020 loss).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less equity compensation less award taxes): FY2020 ~720, FY2022 953.2, FY2025 447.3, TTM Sep-2026 794.3. The decline is growth capex rising from 0.95bn (FY2020) to 3.3bn (FY2025) and ~5bn (FY2026), not deteriorating operations: adjusted EBITDA went 2,901 -> 4,957 over FY2022-FY2025. Equity compensation is under 1% of revenue and under 3% of EBITDA, so owner and reported FCF move together. All periods from TRGP_Metrics.csv and the kpis table.

scenario_narratives.base: The build-out delivers roughly what the last one did. The Permian plants in the 2025-2028 slate (Falcon II, East Pembrook, East Driver, Copperhead, Yeti, Wrangler, Ranger) fill on schedule behind the 20-year ExxonMobil dedications, Speedway and the Galena Park export expansion come on in late 2027, and Mont Belvieu Trains 11-14 take the resulting NGL barrels. Adjusted EBITDA grows about 11% a year through 2028 and slows to low single digits by the early 2030s as Permian gas growth matures. Growth capex steps down from ~5bn in 2026 to ~2bn by 2031, cash tax ramps as the 4.4bn NOL is consumed, and the business is capitalised at about 9x EBITDA at exit.
scenario_narratives.bull: Permian gas and NGL growth keeps outpacing crude for longer than the base case assumes as Blackcomb, Hugh Brinson and Traverse keep Waha basis positive, so Targa's integrated wellhead-to-dock chain earns fee margin on every incremental molecule. The plants and fractionation train currently under evaluation are sanctioned at build multiples near 4x, LPG export docks run full on international demand, and the fee-based mix lifts margins. EBITDA compounds at 12-14% through 2028 and still grows 3% a year at the end of the horizon; the market continues to pay a premium multiple for a de-risked, contract-backed grower.
scenario_narratives.bear: A sustained oil-price downturn slows Permian drilling just as a dozen plants and several pipelines arrive, so new capacity ramps slowly and well connects fail to offset natural declines on the legacy systems. Percent-of-proceeds margin falls with NGL and gas prices, Waha turns negative again, and competitors with spare capacity (Enterprise, Energy Transfer, ONEOK) pressure recontracting. The 2027-2028 capex is committed and gets spent anyway, pushing leverage up while the dividend has just been raised 20%, which forces the buyback off. EBITDA grows only 2-5% a year and the business exits at a commodity-midstream multiple of about 7x EBITDA.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Targa is valued on unlevered owner cash flow built from adjusted-EBITDA and capex dollars, because revenue is mostly commodity pass-through and reported FCF is depressed by a growth programme at roughly 20x maintenance capex. The valuation question is whether ~15bn of 2025-2028 growth capex earns the ~5x build multiple of the previous cycle, and what a buyer pays for the resulting cash flow once growth slows; the terminal value is capped at 15x unlevered FCF (about 9x EBITDA), not the ~14x EBITDA the market pays today. Equity is a levered residual: 19.8bn of net debt sits against the enterprise value, so a one-turn change in the exit EBITDA multiple moves value by roughly $20-25 a share.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is about 55-60% of enterprise value and the cap multiple binds in the base case; each 1x of unlevered-FCF multiple is roughly $13 a share
Leverage: net debt of 19.8bn magnifies every change in enterprise value by about 1.3x at the equity level
Build multiple on the 2025-2028 capex: at 6x rather than ~4.7x the base case loses several hundred million of EBITDA by 2029
Terminal reinvestment: capex is held near D&A; if sustaining the system needs materially more well-connect capital, terminal FCF is overstated
Cash-tax timing: the NOL and bonus depreciation defer tax; a faster ramp to the full rate (or CAMT applying) reduces the 2028-2032 flows
Commodity exposure through percent-of-proceeds contracts is carried in the bear scenario, not in the discount rate
FY0 revenue and EBITDA include a Q4-2026 estimate; replace with actuals at the FY2026 10-K

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 166.18-316.60
data_sources.financials: TRGP_Metrics.csv and the kpis table (SEC XBRL); Q3-2026 10-Q (TRGP_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt) for the debt table, adjusted EBITDA / adjusted FCF reconciliation, growth vs maintenance capex and diluted shares; FY2025 10-K (TRGP_Annual_FY2025.txt) for NOL carryforwards, CAMT and OBBBA tax commentary and lease liabilities
data_sources.qualitative: TRGP_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 guidance, ExxonMobil agreements, project slate, risks

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for Q3 2026 (10-Q EPS note), 215.2m; held FLAT because equity compensation is expensed in the flows. The count has been falling ~1%/yr on repurchases, which is the cash mechanism for the flat count.
inputs.sbc_source: Trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026: 'Compensation on equity grants' 75.9 (FY2025 69.5 less 9M-2025 52.2 plus 9M-2026 58.6, cash flow statement and adjusted EBITDA reconciliation) plus cash taxes on net-share settlement 63.6 (FY2025 67.3 less 9M-2025 63.8 plus 9M-2026 60.1, financing activities). Targa publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per the house rule.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~9.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (recent issuance 4.35% 2031 / 6.05% 2056, investment grade), ~4.4% after tax. Market-value weights ~76% equity / 24% debt -> ~8.3-8.4%; 8.5% used. The same WACC is applied to all three scenarios: commodity, leverage and execution risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt for finance leases: the 684.6 of finance lease liabilities sits inside total debt obligations and no principal is deducted from the flows. Operating leases are small (113.8 at FY2025) and their rent is already an operating cost inside adjusted EBITDA; they are excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, through the flows. Targa's adjusted EBITDA starts from net income attributable to Targa Resources Corp. and its capex figures are net of contributions from noncontrolling interests, so the driver paths are attributable-only. The 144.9 noncontrolling-interest balance (WestTX JV partner and others) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company route, with the cyclical/NCI/lease adaptations). Targa is a C-corp operating midstream business whose value is unlevered cash flow from gathering, processing, NGL transport, fractionation and export; it is not a REIT, trust or pass-through, so EBITDA less tax and capex discounted at WACC with consolidated debt deducted is the right frame. REVENUE IS A CARRIER: 83% of revenue is commodity pass-through, so revenue is not the economic driver. The paths are built in adjusted-EBITDA dollars and capex dollars and then expressed as growth x margin and capex % of revenue; read the EBITDA and capex dollar lines, not the revenue line. FY0 IS AN ESTIMATE: base_revenue 19,300 is 9M-2026 actual 14,133.4 plus a Q4 estimate; FY2026E adjusted EBITDA 6,050 (guidance 'at least 6.0bn', 9M actual 4,510.1) is 31.35% of it. Year 1 is calendar FY2027. STUB: the balance sheet is 30 Sep 2026, so the Q4-2026 unlevered flow (EBITDA ~1,550 less remaining guided capex ~1,870) is carried in the equity bridge rather than dropped. NET DEBT uses face value: reported total debt obligations 19,844.5 plus 124.4 unamortised issuance costs, less cash 142.6. last_fcf and reported_fcf are TRAILING TWELVE MONTHS to 30 Sep 2026 on the reported (levered, after growth capex) basis: OCF less capex 933.8, less equity compensation and award taxes 139.5. That figure is depressed by a growth capex programme running at roughly 20x maintenance capex and is not a steady-state earnings measure; management's adjusted cash flow from operations (before growth capex) was 3,827.7 for 9M-2026. BUYBACKS: 224.1 TTM, an actual repurchaser, so the flat count is funded. CASH TAX: US federal NOL carryforwards of 4.4bn at FY2025 plus permanent 100% bonus depreciation (OBBBA) on a ~5bn/yr build keep cash tax near zero (1.1 for 9M-2026); the path ramps to a 22% full rate by year 9 and the terminal year carries no shelter. Not reflected: the contested 47.8 New Mexico penalty and the FERC Badlands tariff dispute, both under $0.25/share. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.rationale: EBITDA ~6,180 FY2027 -> ~6,320 FY2028 -> ~6,400 FY2029 -> ~7,170 FY2036. The FY2027-FY2028 capex is already committed (~4.2bn and ~3.3bn) and is spent into a slower basin, so the build earns well under 5x; capex then falls to ~1.8-1.9bn. Lower income stretches the NOL, so cash tax arrives later.

base.rationale: EBITDA dollars: 6,050 (FY2026E) -> ~6,750 FY2027 -> ~7,540 FY2028 -> ~8,270 FY2029 -> ~10,770 FY2036. Capex dollars (growth + maintenance): ~4.2bn, 3.5bn, 2.9bn, 2.6bn, 2.4bn, then ~2.3bn. Cumulative FY2025-FY2028 growth capex of ~15bn against ~3.3bn of added EBITDA is ~4.7x, in line with the ~5x Targa earned on FY2022-FY2025 spend. Terminal capex (7.0% of revenue, ~2.3bn) is held close to D&A (~2.4bn) because gathering systems need continuous well-connect capital that Targa classes as growth. Cap of 15x unlevered FCF binds (Gordon is 15.7x) and equates to ~9x terminal EBITDA.

bull.rationale: EBITDA ~7,040 FY2027 -> ~8,060 FY2028 -> ~8,990 FY2029 -> ~12,600 FY2036. Capex stays higher for longer (~4.5bn, 4.0bn, 3.4bn, 3.0bn) because the additional plants and fractionation train under evaluation get sanctioned; cash tax arrives sooner on higher income.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): debt is rising ~2.5bn a year into a committed multi-year build while the dividend is being raised 20%, and a commodity downturn would hit drilling activity and percent-of-proceeds margin together. Base 50%: guidance has been raised through 2026 and the ExxonMobil dedications make the next two years of volume unusually visible. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs Permian gas growth, export demand and low build multiples to all persist beyond the currently sanctioned slate.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
